question: Did GET /users/me really regress 8->16 ms p50 and 19->740 ms p95 across 4cd00654..7de0ff2a? Judged on the DELTA between two arms under one instrument, NOT against the stored CSVs, which the plan disqualifies.

loop_lag.instrument: harness-owned loop-lag sampler (NOT T-1: T-1 does not exist in either arm)

before.server_instrument: harness-owned TimingMiddleware (NOT T-3: absent from both arms)

after.loop_lag_note: /home/ansible/ab/after_arm.json was not written. The lag histogram is the mechanism the plan names, so a missing one is stated rather than assumed fine.

delta.verdict: NULL RESULT: no delta exceeds the noise floor
delta.detail: Neither view reaches the intra-arm floor. The claimed 39x does not reproduce, and the plan treats a null as a valid and valuable result.

gate_a_compliance.3_loop_lag_histogram: read from each arm's instrument export; see loop_lag

4_separate_load_host.deviation: UNSATISFIABLE in this environment. perf-app and perf-load are both TCP-unreachable and only one host exists. Recorded here in the vocabulary GATE A(5) provides for exactly this case. What IS delivered is the substance of (4): server-side AND client-observed both reported per arm, so generator starvation shows up as a client-minus-server gap instead of as a fake regression.

gate_a_compliance.5_production_budgets: No control was relaxed. At tier pro the budget is (1000, 3600) per user per path and this run issues ~156 per account, so no arm can be starved by the other; GATE A(6) is then satisfied by asserting zero non-200 rather than by trusting a purge.

instrument.why: Measured: neither arm contains request_timer.py, so no in-app timer can be imported. Owning the instrument outside both trees is what guarantees neither arm carries a different one.
